bodyHtml:
If you are in need of help, look for an inpatient alcohol rehab near you to find an inpatient treatment program that will give you the tools you need to succeed long term.

What is Inpatient Treatment?

If you are ready to find an inpatient alcohol rehab near me, you have to find a program that gives you what you need most: long-term chances of success.

Inpatient alcohol rehab treatment means you live at the recovery facility where you receive medical detoxification during your initial stages of recovery followed by long-term therapy and holistic treatments so that you have the tools to kick your addiction permanently.

How is Inpatient Treatment Used to Treat Alcoholism?

Inpatient alcohol rehab can treat multiple levels of alcoholism.

Detox

Inpatient treatment starts with detoxification. For those struggling with alcoholism, the body becomes physically reliant on it, making it next to impossible to quit on your own. Inpatient treatment helps you overcome the initial symptoms of alcohol withdrawal under medical supervision so that the severity of your symptoms can be medically managed, keeping you as comfortable as possible.

Long Term Therapy

Long-term therapy can take place over 30 days, 60 days, or 90 days depending on the alcohol rehab program selected. The longer you undergo treatment, the higher your chances of success. Long-term therapy includes one-on-one therapy, group counseling, maybe even family therapy, depending on what you need most.

Holistic Tools

Holistic tools are used in conjunction with evidence-based practice to give you long-term coping strategies to overcome stress, anger, that communication, or unhelpful environments. Rather than turning back to alcohol, holistic tools give you alternate events so that you can stay sober longer.

Is Inpatient Rehab Right For Me?

When finding an inpatient alcohol rehab near me, you need to figure out if inpatient treatment for alcohol is best for your situation.

Supportive Environment

Inpatient alcohol rehab might be the best solution for you if you don’t have a supportive environment at home. Some people have family or partners who do not support the decision to get clean, while others have high-stress daily lives that are full of triggers leading to alcohol abuse.

If you need a supportive environment where you can get the necessary treatment and support staff who want you to succeed, inpatient treatment might be best.

Dual Diagnosis

For many people, alcohol addiction is just one part of the picture. Substance abuse and alcoholism often have underlying untreated medical conditions, dressers or triggers in daily life, or other addictions that need to be tackled simultaneously.

A good inpatient treatment will offer dual diagnosis opportunities so you can treat your alcoholism as well as conditions like depression or anxiety.

Customized Therapy

No two people are the same, and no two inpatient treatments should be the same either. If you want customized inpatient rehab for your alcoholism, with a program designed specifically to meet your needs, an inpatient program is going to be much better than an outpatient program. Inpatient treatment programs can help you get family therapy if your family is a contributor to your alcoholism. Inpatient alcohol rehab can customize holistic treatments by incorporating yoga, meditation, and other exercise programs for when life gets too stressful.
